items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: Clarence contacted me a few days after I arrived and I started working with him doing one-night stands in Kentucky, West Virginia and Ohio.

ctx.x: Clarence Page played in the Sterling Hotel in the winter. The Sterling was on 6th and Mound Streets and had been a big time white hotel at one time. More and more negro people started to come to Cincinnati from the Southern states and this part of the city called Downtown was where they found homes and places of entertainment. There was a gambling house on 5th Street between John and Central Avenue which was run by a man named Ed Gaither. He later opened another one in Carlisle Avenue and Mount Street. My mother…

The Sterling Hotel had big dances in the winter and I could hear the music coming from the ballroom from outside, but it was not as interesting as in the summer when Clarence would play in Sinton Park.

I was 14 years old when a man by the name of Ernest Moore, who used to play in the band with my father, Uncle Ernest and Uncle John in Centerville and was now living in Cincinnati, started a band to teach young boys to play music; and I joined this band. I never knew how Mr. Ernest Moore managed to do what he was doing, because he was not a rich man and he did not charge for teaching the boys.
